items.title: Inquest set for 88-year-old who died after well-being check by Peel police in 2023

items.title: Marten Falls First Nation and Bird Construction Expand Piinahzii LP Partnership Agreement to Include Construction of the Marten Falls Community Access Road
items.summary: This content may have been approved or produced by a partner MISSISSAUGA, Ontario, Aug. 31, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Bird Construction Inc. (TSX: BDT) announced today that Piinahzii Limited Partnership (“Piinahzii LP”) has signed an agreement to expand the scope of the partnership to include the Marten Falls Community Access Road. Piinahzii LP is a majority Indigenous-owned partnership formed by Marten Falls First Nation and Bird earlier this year. MISSISSAUGA, Ontario, Aug. 31, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Bird Construction Inc. (TSX: BDT) announced today that Piinahzii Limited Partnership (“Piinahzii LP”) has signed an agreement to expand the scope of the partnership to include the Marten Falls Community Access Road. Piinahzii LP is a majority Indigenous-owned partnership formed by Marten Falls First Nation and Bird earlier this year. Aligned with the recent announcement by the Province of Ontario marking the ground breaking for the Marten Falls Community Access Road, the amended agreement expands Piinahzii LP’s role beyond community infrastructure and readiness work, to include construction of the access road itself. The agreement builds on the existing framework for jointly pursuing and executing infrastructure projects within the community and the Marten Falls First Nation Traditional Territory, while creating employment, training and contracting opportunities for community members and businesses. The Marten Falls Community Access Road will connect Marten Falls First Nation to Ontario’s provincial highway network for the first time, providing reliable year-round access to health care, education, essential services, and economic opportunities. At approximately 184 kilometres and including 35 bridge and culvert structures, it is the longest segment of the proposed 514 kilometre all season road network being advanced to support access to the Ring of Fire region.

items.title: Barrie man facing multiple charges was arrested in Mississauga
items.summary: A 50-year-old Barrie man who is facing multiple charges in connection with a human trafficking investigation was arrested in Mississauga, police say. Barrie police said that in June, officers received information about a Barrie man who was allegedly recruiting females to provide sexual services for an escort service out of his home. Police subsequently identified online ads for sexual services linked to the suspect, officers said. Earlier this month, on Aug. 12, officers executed a search warrant related to the case at an address in Springwater Township. And this past Sunday, Michael Brocklebank was arrested in Mississauga “without incident,” police said. Brocklebank is now facing multiple charges including trafficking in persons, material benefit from trafficking in persons, material benefit from sexual services, advertising sexual services, assault, and procuring — exercising control, direction, or influence. He was also charged with failing to comply with a probation order.

items.title: Street festival for the dogs and their parents happening in Mississauga
items.summary: A Mississauga street will be transformed for a festival just for the dogs and their parents. Toronto Dog Moms hosts Dogsville 2026, their biggest event ever in celebration of Toronto Dog Mom Day on Saturday, Sept. 26. Mississauga’s Streetsville Village Square will become a dog-friendly street festival bringing hundreds of dog parents, animal lovers and pet-friendly businesses together for an afternoon of community, entertainment and adorable pups, according to Toronto Dog Moms. The festival includes local vendors, live entertainment, interactive experiences, photo ops and community activations. The family-friendly event will give pet parents the chance to bond with their dogs, connect with fellow dog lovers and support small businesses. Toronto Dog Moms is partnering with Music Day in Canada for a line-up of musicians, which includes Veneice, Gracie Ella, Avery, Neddy and Jennie Law. m. m. on Sept. 26 in Streetsville Village Square at 213 Queen St. S. The event is free. For more information, see the Eventbrite page here.

items.title: Weather system could bring heavy rain and thunderstorms to Mississauga
items.summary: Residents are urged to stay alert as a weather system moves through Mississauga today, bringing the risk of heavy rain, thunderstorms, and possible watershed flooding. Emergency and public safety | August 31, 2026 A weather system moving through southern Ontario is expected to bring additional rainfall and thunderstorms to Mississauga this afternoon and evening. The Toronto and Region Conservation Authority (TRCA) and Credit Valley Conservation (CVC) are advising residents to prepare for changing weather conditions. For safety, residents are urged to: With soils already saturated and water levels elevated, rivers, streams and stormwater systems may respond quickly to additional rainfall. TRCA advises that river and stream water levels are already high and are expected to continue rising over the next 24 hours. Watercourses have not yet reached their peak levels and stronger, faster flows are expected throughout the day and into tomorrow. items.title: House of the week: Mississauga home comes with pool and separate entrance
items.summary: This place: Large family home with a pool and a separate entrance in Mississauga. Features: This home offers over 7,100 square feet of living space across three finished levels. Features include 10-foot ceilings on the main level, nine-foot ceilings upstairs and in the basement, solid pine plank flooring, custom millwork, two staircases and a curved bow window. The kitchen boasts granite countertops, Wolf appliances, a Sub-Zero refrigerator, a centre island, a butler’s pantry and a walk-in wine room. The kitchen connects to the family room, which is anchored by a gas fireplace and overlooks the backyard. The primary bedroom upstairs features a six-piece ensuite bathroom and a dressing room. The four additional upstairs bedrooms have ensuite or semi-ensuite bathroom access. The separate entrance to the basement leads to a recreation lounge, a wet bar, a home theatre, a sixth bedroom and a full bathroom. Outside, find a new pool, hot tub, covered pergola with a wood-burning fireplace, a built-in barbecue, retractable awning, professional landscaping, landscape lighting and an irrigation system. This home is near Mississauga Golf and Country Club, Port Credit Village, Clarkson Village, University of Toronto Mississauga, Trillium Health Partners, Riverwood Conservancy, Erindale Park, Rattray Marsh Conservation Area, Culham Trail, the QEW, Highway 403 and GO Transit. Thanks to Sam McDadi Real Estate Inc. Brokerage for all the information about the House of the Week. For more information about this house, please visit Sam McDadi Real Estate Inc. Brokerage.

items.title: New $1.3B hospital almost halfway complete in Toronto, near Mississauga
items.summary: 3-billion hospital in Toronto’s west end just steps from Mississauga is almost halfway complete, officials say. The new Gilgan Family Queensway Health Centre in Etobicoke, being funded largely by the province via Infrastructure Ontario, is scheduled to open in 2029. -ft. Gilgan Family Queensway Health Centre will include a new patient tower described earlier by hospital officials as a modern nine-story facility with more than 350 beds and fully private patient rooms to ensure privacy and enhance infection prevention control. Work began in February 2024 and the new hospital, which is part of the Trillium Health Partners health-care network that also includes Mississauga and Credit Valley hospitals, will serve the rapidly growing needs of fast-growing communities, now and in the future, Ontario Premier Doug Ford said earlier. ” Mississauga-based EllisDon is building The Gilgan Family Queensway Health Centre, which when open will “increase our hospital’s capacity to provide quality health care from Milton to Toronto,” THP officials said in 2024.

items.title: Branch out and explore nature at National Forest Week and fall events
items.summary: Mississauga’s National Forest Week and fall events programming takes root September 19 to November 7. Entertainment and activities | August 31, 2026 National Forest Week and fall events highlight the important role trees play in creating resilient communities. Residents are invited to connect with nature, learn from forestry experts and discover the many benefits of Mississauga’s urban forest. From cleaner air and cooler neighbourhoods to enhanced biodiversity and community well-being, trees play an important role in keeping our city healthy and green. Mississauga’s urban forest is a network of natural spaces that provide habitat for wildlife, improve air quality, reduce summer heat and create healthier neighbourhoods. National Forest Week and fall events programming gets to the root of what makes the city green. Whether you’re planting a tree, discovering local wildlife on a guided walk or picking up a free tree for your yard, the events offer fun, educational and hands-on experiences for all ages. The second annual Forestry Fall Festival returns to Erindale Park with a day of family-friendly activities, packed with trees, treats, tractor-sized fun and community spirit. There’s something for everyone at the festival. Enjoy horse-drawn wagon rides, explore reptile and snake exhibits, plant a tree, and learn how Mississauga’s urban forest is cared for. Meet the forestry experts behind the work and get an up-close look at the specialized equipment they use to keep things growing and healthy.

Erindale Park Braces for Road Closures as It Hosts One of Canada's Largest Comedy Festivals
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, Erindale Park will host the Great Outdoors Comedy Festival from September 11 to 13, marking the first time the park has hosted one of the largest comedy festivals in the country. The city says the weekend lineup includes live stand-up from Emmy-winning and acclaimed comedians performing against the backdrop of the Credit River. According to the city, tickets remain available for all three days through the festival's website. The city reports temporary closures will affect Erindale Park and the surrounding area from September 6 to 16 to support event setup, operations and teardown. According to the city, Dundas Street West will be reduced to one lane of traffic in each direction between Mississauga Road and Robinson Street during parts of that period, with a temporary crosswalk staffed by police set up across from the park's main entrance.
